label: violation
variant_strategy: single sentence, corporate email genre
text: This quarter's rebrand marks a pivotal moment in our company's journey toward global relevance.
rationale: Uses stock inflation language ('marks a pivotal moment') to overstate the importance of a routine rebrand.

label: violation
variant_strategy: product launch tweet, breathless tone
text: This isn't just a blender, it's a REVOLUTIONARY leap in kitchen technology that will change how you eat forever!!!
rationale: Excessive exclamation and words like 'revolutionary' inflate a mundane appliance into a life-changing breakthrough.

label: violation
variant_strategy: meeting recap, dense buzzword stacking
text: Let's circle back next sprint to leverage synergies across teams so we can really move the needle on Q3 deliverables.
rationale: Stacks empty corporate buzzwords ('circle back', 'leverage synergies', 'move the needle') without concrete content.

label: violation
variant_strategy: health article, uncited claim
text: Experts agree that walking after meals improves digestion, and studies show it can lower blood sugar spikes significantly.
rationale: Cites unnamed 'experts' and 'studies' with no source or specific figures to back the claim.

label: violation
variant_strategy: chatbot answer, hedged temporal caveat
text: As of my last update, I don't have real-time access to current stock prices, so I can't confirm today's closing figures for you.
rationale: Classic AI disclaimer phrasing about knowledge cutoffs and lack of live access, out of place in most human writing.

label: violation
variant_strategy: essay opener, throat-clearing preamble
text: It is worth noting that, when considering the topic at hand, there are several factors that come into play regarding urban planning.
rationale: The sentence adds no actual content, just empty preamble phrases that delay getting to a point.

label: violation
variant_strategy: news-style report, stacked qualifiers
text: It's important to note that the policy could potentially lead to changes that may possibly affect some residents in certain areas.
rationale: Piles on hedges ('could potentially', 'may possibly', 'some', 'certain') until the sentence says almost nothing.

label: violation
variant_strategy: opinion piece, forced two-sides framing
text: On one hand, eating vegetables is good for you; on the other hand, some people simply prefer the taste of pizza.
rationale: Manufactures a false equivalence between a health claim and a taste preference, presenting no genuine tension.

label: violation
variant_strategy: self-help closing line, false depth reversal
text: In the end, running a marathon isn't really about crossing the finish line, it's about the person you become along the way.
rationale: Uses the 'it's not about X, it's about Y' template to manufacture emotional depth from a cliche.

label: violation
variant_strategy: review post, staged honesty framing
text: I'll be honest, this laptop isn't perfect, but let's be real, for the price, it gets the job done pretty well.
rationale: The candour markers ('I'll be honest', 'let's be real') are performative flourishes rather than genuine disclosure of anything surprising.

label: violation
variant_strategy: blog intro, generic scene-setting opener
text: In today's fast-paced world, staying organized has never been more important, and in conclusion, a good planner can help.
rationale: Opens and closes with stock formulaic phrases ('in today's fast-paced world', 'in conclusion') that could preface any topic.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: paraphrased with contraction and reordered clause
text: We're at a real turning point with the shop lease, so I want everyone's read on it before Friday.
rationale: Conveys 'pivotal moment' style urgency but grounds it in a specific, concrete situation with plain, unforced wording.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: casual dialogue with natural contractions
text: I dunno, the coach said we'll probably start Sarah at forward if her ankle's healed by Saturday.
rationale: Contractions and casual filler ('I dunno') reflect authentic spoken register, not a tell.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: British spelling variant in narrative prose
text: The colour of the harbour at dusk in Cornwall reminded her of the watercolours her grandmother used to paint.
rationale: British spellings ('colour', 'harbour', 'watercolours') are a normal regional variant, not evidence of AI generation.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: near-miss sentence that looks like a tell but is specific and grounded
text: The 1918 armistice mattered less for ending the fighting than for the reparations debate it triggered at Versailles a year later.
rationale: Resembles the 'not about X, it's about Y' pattern superficially but makes a specific, sourced historical claim rather than vague uplift.

label: violation
variant_strategy: classic 'not just X, it's Y' template applied to a product pitch
text: This isn't just a water bottle, it's a statement. It isn't about hydration, it's about identity.
rationale: The rigid 'not just X, it's Y' scaffolding repeated twice signals formulaic AI phrasing rather than a writer building a genuine contrast.

label: violation
variant_strategy: three consecutive sentences opening with 'This' in a policy summary
text: This marks the third rate hike this year. This follows months of pressure from lenders. This suggests the central bank sees inflation as still unresolved.
rationale: Three sentences in a row starting with 'This' as a vague pointer is a well-documented syntactic tic of generated text, not a stylistic choice a human editor would let stand.

label: violation
variant_strategy: dangling participle opener faking analytical depth in a report summary
text: Highlighting the urgency of the situation, the audit found three servers running unpatched software.
rationale: The participial phrase asserts significance without doing any actual analytical work, a shortcut common in generated summaries.

label: violation
variant_strategy: unclear referent for 'this' and 'that said' in a book review closing
text: This matters more than it seems. That said, the pacing drags in the middle chapters.
rationale: The demonstrative 'this' has no clear antecedent, letting the sentence sound weighty while asserting nothing specific.

label: violation
variant_strategy: clipped fragment run for false emphasis in a motivational blurb
text: Wake up early. Drink water. Move your body. Success follows.
rationale: The uniform two-to-three word commands create rhythmic punch without earning it through content, a hallmark of generated inspirational copy.

label: violation
variant_strategy: repeated 'We believe' opener across a mission statement
text: We believe in innovation. We believe in transparency. We believe in putting people first.
rationale: The mechanical repetition of an identical stem across three flat clauses substitutes cadence for substance, typical of generated brand copy.

label: violation
variant_strategy: self-answered question used as a crutch in an explainer
text: So why does this matter? Because it changes how millions of people commute every day.
rationale: The question exists only to be immediately answered by the writer, a scripted device rather than genuine inquiry.

label: violation
variant_strategy: formulaic rule-of-three adjective list in a product description
text: Our new blender is faster, smarter, and quieter than anything on the market.
rationale: The three-adjective list is a stock rhetorical mold applied without any specific evidence behind each claim.

label: violation
variant_strategy: every sentence identical subject-verb-object length in a travel snippet
text: The city has old buildings. The streets have narrow alleys. The markets have fresh produce. The people have warm smiles.
rationale: Four sentences of near-identical length and syntax with no variation in structure read as machine-generated cadence rather than natural prose.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: short punchy sentence followed by a long one, genuinely motivated by content
text: My father never raised his voice. It was the silences that scared me, the long pauses before he decided whether something was worth forgiving.
rationale: The short-then-long pairing mirrors the actual emotional beat being described rather than imposing rhythm for its own sake.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: legitimate interrupting clause carrying real qualifying information
text: The comet, which last passed near Earth in 1986, will not return for another seventy-five years.
rationale: The relative clause adds a specific, necessary fact rather than padding, making it a natural interruption instead of a stylistic tic.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: sentence led by an unusual abstract subject instead of a person
text: Whatever guilt survives a divorce tends to outlive the marriage itself.
rationale: Fronting an abstract noun phrase as the subject is a legitimate stylistic move a skilled writer makes deliberately, not a formulaic tell.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: semicolon joining two balanced but distinct observations
text: The soup arrived lukewarm; the bread, at least, was still warm from the oven.
rationale: The semicolon links two contrasting but concrete observations with genuine content on each side, not a formulaic dash-for-drama pattern.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: recast of a stock rhetorical question into a direct statement
text: People keep asking whether remote work killed office culture, but the culture was already thinning out well before anyone went home.
rationale: The question is folded into a subordinate clause and immediately complicated with a specific counterpoint, avoiding the ask-then-answer crutch.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: near-miss triad that is actually a specific, unforced list
text: "I need the invoice, the shipping label, and whatever's left of my patience," she said, already reaching for her coat.
rationale: The three items superficially resemble a rhetorical triad but are concrete, unequal in register, and grounded in a specific dramatic moment rather than rhythmic parallelism.

label: violation
variant_strategy: overuse across a short chat message for rhythmic emphasis
text: I looked at the logs — and honestly — the issue isn't the database, it's the retry logic — which keeps firing every two seconds — so we need to fix that first.
rationale: Four em dashes in one short message create an artificial staccato rhythm that reads as machine-generated emphasis rather than natural pausing.

label: violation
variant_strategy: arrows and sparkle symbols used as ornamental section markers in a wiki page
text:
✦ Project Status ✦

→ Backend: stable
→ Frontend: in progress
→ Docs: pending

✦ Next Steps ✦

→ Ship the auth flow by Friday
rationale: The sparkle and arrow glyphs add no information and function purely as decorative flourish, a common tell of generated status updates.

label: violation
variant_strategy: ordinary nouns and verbs bolded throughout a short paragraph
text: This library **helps** you **parse** configuration files **quickly**. It **supports** YAML, JSON, and TOML, and it **works** with **Node** and **Deno** out of the box.
rationale: Bolding common verbs and nouns with no contrastive purpose is emphasis inflation rather than genuine highlighting of key terms.

label: violation
variant_strategy: formulaic Label: description pattern repeated for every bullet in a product spec
text:
- **Scope:** covers the checkout flow only
- **Timeline:** four weeks from kickoff
- **Owner:** the payments team
- **Risk:** third-party API rate limits
- **Dependency:** the new tax service
rationale: Every item follows the identical bolded-noun-colon template, a rigid pattern rarely seen in human-drafted specs which vary phrasing and structure.

label: violation
variant_strategy: heading syntax inserted into a casual Slack-style message
text:
## Lunch plans

Thinking tacos today, anyone in? Let me know by 11:30 so I can get a headcount for the order.
rationale: A level-2 heading in a two-sentence casual message is structurally unnecessary and signals templated generation rather than informal human typing.

label: violation
variant_strategy: mini bolded headings shoved inside parentheses mid-paragraph
text: We reviewed the vendor contract yesterday (key concern: the renewal clause auto-extends unless we cancel 90 days out) and flagged it for legal (action needed: confirm cancellation deadline) before signing.
rationale: Embedding label-like fragments in parentheses mimics heading structure without committing to real formatting, a hedge pattern typical of generated text.

label: violation
variant_strategy: the word Note: reused three times as a structural crutch in one paragraph
text: Note: the API key must be set before startup. Note: rate limits reset hourly, not daily. Note: sandbox mode ignores billing entirely, so test freely there.
rationale: Repeating the same label word to introduce every sentence substitutes for actual transitions or prose flow, a mechanical crutch rather than natural writing.

label: violation
variant_strategy: converting a naturally flowing narrative paragraph into an unnecessary bulleted list
text:
Why we're switching vendors:
- The old vendor raised prices twice this year
- Support tickets take five days to get a reply
- Their uptime dropped below 99% last quarter
- The new vendor offered a better contract
rationale: This content reads naturally as connected reasoning and gains nothing from fragmentation into bullets, a hallmark of over-listing generated content.

label: violation
variant_strategy: three paragraphs of near-identical length and sentence count in a blog-style piece
text: The first quarter brought steady growth across our core markets, with new signups outpacing churn for the first time in a year. The second quarter saw a slight dip as seasonal demand cooled, though retention held firm. The third quarter rebounded sharply, driven largely by a product update that resonated well with existing users.
rationale: Each paragraph runs to almost exactly the same length and clause structure, an unnatural uniformity rarely produced by a human writer moving through varied content.

label: violation
variant_strategy: a short summary sentence tacked onto the end of every paragraph in a report
text: Sales in the northern region grew 12% this quarter, driven by a new distributor partnership. In summary, the north performed well. Meanwhile, the southern region held flat as two major accounts paused orders. In summary, the south remained stable overall.
rationale: Appending a miniature wrap-up to every paragraph, even short ones with no complexity to summarize, is a repetitive tic rather than a natural writing choice.

label: violation
variant_strategy: leftover bracketed template text left in a document presented as finished
text: Hi team, please find attached the final Q3 report. Revenue grew [insert percentage here] compared to last quarter, largely due to [insert driver here]. Let me know if you have questions before we present Friday.
rationale: Unfilled template placeholders in a message described as final are leftover scaffolding, a clear sign the text was never fully completed or reviewed.

label: violation
variant_strategy: leftover conversational assistant phrasing left inside a document body
text: Deployment steps: build the image, push to the registry, then run the migration script. I've updated the section above to reflect the new registry URL. Let me know if you'd like me to adjust the rollback steps too.
rationale: The trailing offer to adjust further and the reference to having updated a section are conversational residue from an assistant interaction, not content meant for a standalone wiki page.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: a single purposeful heading and bold term aiding scanability in technical docs
text:
## Rate limiting

Requests are capped at **100 per minute** per API key. Exceeding this returns a 429 status; retry after the `Retry-After` header value has elapsed.
rationale: The heading marks a genuine section boundary in a longer doc and the single bold figure highlights the one number readers need to find quickly, both functional rather than decorative.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: a naturally occurring numbered list in a genre where sequence is inherent
text:
1. Preheat the oven to 200C.
2. Toss the potatoes in oil and salt.
3. Roast for 35 minutes, turning once halfway through.
4. Rest for five minutes before serving.
rationale: Numbered steps are the standard, expected convention for recipes since the sequence and order genuinely matter, unlike numbering imposed on non-sequential content.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: label-colon pattern that looks like bold-label lists but is legitimate legal clause formatting
text: Definitions. "Effective Date" means the date first written above. "Services" means the consulting work described in Exhibit A. "Term" means the period beginning on the Effective Date and ending as set out in Section 4.
rationale: This resembles the bold-label-list tell superficially but is standard legal drafting convention for defined terms, functional and expected in this genre rather than a formulaic AI crutch.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: classic tricolon used for rhetorical emphasis in a scholarly argument, not filler padding
text: The reform failed for three intertwined reasons: weak enforcement, insufficient funding, and a judiciary unwilling to intervene. Each factor alone might have been survivable; together they were fatal.
rationale: Tricolon structure is a long-standing rhetorical device in academic prose for signalling a causal argument with parallel weight, not a generic AI list habit.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: opinion-column rhetorical question driving reader engagement, a standard journalistic device
text: So why did the council approve a budget it knew it couldn't fund? Interviews with three former staffers suggest the answer lies less in arithmetic than in politics.
rationale: Rhetorical questions are a staple of feature and opinion journalism used to pivot into investigative framing, and predate AI text generation by decades.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: API reference parameters genuinely require bolded field names for scanability
text:
**timeout**: maximum wait in milliseconds before the request aborts.
**retries**: number of attempts after the first failure.
**backoff**: multiplier applied between retries.
rationale: Bolded parameter names in API docs are a decades-old documentation convention (see man pages, RFCs, javadoc) required for skimmability, not an AI tic.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: clipped stage direction rhythm in a screenplay, anaphoric by design for pacing
text:
INT. WAREHOUSE - NIGHT
This is the last crate. This is the last chance. This is where it ends, one way or another.
rationale: Anaphoric 'This is' openings are a deliberate screenwriting technique for building tension in stage direction and monologue, a convention older than any language model.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: interruptive em dash conveying a character's broken train of thought, a literary staple
text: She reached for the letter—stopped—and let her hand fall back into her lap, as if the paper might burn her fingers if she were foolish enough to touch it.
rationale: Em dashes signalling interrupted action or thought are a core technique in literary prose going back to Dickinson and Woolf, not a marker of machine generation.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: a real scientist's cautious, qualified speech pattern in an interview quote
genre: attributed quotation (real or realistic quoted speech)
text: "I think it's probably too early to say whether this holds up," Dr. Okafor told reporters. "We'd want to see it replicated before anyone gets excited."
rationale: Scientists routinely hedge in interviews to avoid overclaiming; this caution is a genuine epistemic norm of scientific speech, not a generated hallmark.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: a grading rubric legitimately enumerates many discrete criteria for consistent scoring
text: 5 points: thesis is clear and arguable. 5 points: evidence supports each claim. 3 points: counterargument addressed. 2 points: citations formatted correctly. 5 points: prose is coherent.
rationale: Long itemised point breakdowns are how rubrics function structurally, enabling consistent grading across markers, not a symptom of formulaic generation.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: standard formal-report section transition required by institutional reporting convention
text: Having outlined the quarter's revenue shortfall, we now turn to the mitigating actions taken by the finance committee in response.
rationale: Formal reports conventionally use explicit signposting transitions between sections for readers skimming to specific findings; this is expected corporate/institutional style, not an AI tell.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: boilerplate legal disclaimer intentionally references generic authorities by design, not because it's evasive
text: This agreement is governed by applicable local, state, and federal law. Consult a qualified professional regarding your specific jurisdiction before signing.
rationale: Boilerplate contracts deliberately use generic authority references because they must apply across jurisdictions; specificity would make the template legally unusable.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: a genuine limitations section from a published study, hedged because the sample truly was small
text: Our sample size (n=42) limits statistical power, and participants were recruited from a single urban clinic, so results may not generalize to rural populations.
rationale: Limitations sections are a required, genre-mandated part of empirical papers where honest hedging about sample size and generalizability is the actual methodological norm.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: a recipe card genuinely needs short headings even though the whole document is brief
text:
## Ingredients
2 cups flour, 1 tsp salt
## Method
Mix dry ingredients, then knead for 8 minutes.
rationale: Recipes conventionally use headings to separate ingredients from method regardless of overall document length; this is a functional convention of the genre, not padding.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: deliberate anaphoric repetition building a historiographical argument, a classic rhetorical figure in academic prose
text: Where the earlier historians saw continuity, we see rupture. Where they saw consensus, we see contested memory. Where they saw an ending, we argue the conflict never resolved.
rationale: Anaphora ('Where they saw... we see') is a recognized rhetorical figure used in academic argumentation to sharpen contrast between interpretive schools, dating to classical rhetoric.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: sports commentary triad summarising a player's performance, a genre-typical cadence
text: He was faster, stronger, and hungrier than anyone else on the pitch tonight, and it showed in every challenge he won.
rationale: Triadic praise is a long-standing rhythm in sportswriting for punchy, quotable summary sentences, unrelated to any generative-model pattern.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: a troubleshooting guide's closing summary genuinely needs a tidy recap for the reader who skipped ahead
text: In summary: check the cable, restart the router, and confirm the firmware version before contacting support.
rationale: Technical guides routinely close with a compact recap so readers who jumped to the end get the full checklist; this closure serves a functional purpose rather than signalling formulaic generation.

label: legitimate_control
variant_strategy: an em dash used in a formal report to insert a necessary aside about data provenance
text: Revenue rose 6 percent year over year—driven largely by the acquisition completed in March—though organic growth remained flat.
rationale: Em dashes are an accepted way in formal business reporting to insert a clarifying aside without breaking the sentence into fragments, a standard tool of concise report writing.
